Argostoli Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Argostoli, Greece

Demolished. The first Jews on Cephalonia settled in Achelous in the 12th-13th centuries; the island's governor brought more Jews in the 17th century to develop its bookbinding industry, most settling in the capital, Argostoli. Post-1821 Greek revolution violence drove further Jewish settlement fleeing antisemitism elsewhere; population reached 130 (of 53,090 total) by 1823. Following Greece's 1864 annexation of Cephalonia, the community's financial position deteriorated through the 1890s, leading to disengagement and eventual dismantlement; only 18 Jews remained by 1907, and just one by 1940. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown, presumed to date to the 17th century.
